subject: Human Evolution
title: Dubois and Java Man
description: A quick, practical guide to Dubois and Java Man.

hook.text: Dutch doctor Eugène Dubois quit his job in 1887 and sailed to Indonesia to find the 'missing link.'

buildup.text: On Java, he found a skullcap, a tooth, and a thighbone along the Solo River in 1891.

discovery.text: He named it Pithecanthropus erectus—'upright ape-man.' Now called Homo erectus, it was a real link.

twist.text: Scientists mocked him. Dubois grew so bitter he hid the fossils under his dining room floor.

climax.text: Decades later, more Homo erectus finds proved Dubois right. He'd found a key human ancestor.

punchline.text: He bet his career on a hunch and won.

quiz.question: What did Eugène Dubois discover in Java?
